name: Cleidocranial Dysplasia and Isolated Cranial Ossification Defect
aliases: Cleidocranial Dysostosis with Cranial Ossification Defect
CCD with Isolated Cranial Ossification Abnormality

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Cleidocranial Dysplasia

criteria.description: Hypoplasia or aplasia of one or both clavicles confirmed by radiography
Delayed closure of anterior fontanelle and presence of wormian bones in cranial sutures
Multiple supernumerary teeth and delayed eruption of permanent teeth
Radiological evidence of isolated cranial ossification defects without other skeletal abnormalities
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of clavicular hypoplasia or aplasia plus delayed closure of cranial fontanelles with or without dental abnormalities
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing for RUNX2 mutations can confirm diagnosis but is not mandatory.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Delayed closure of anterior fontanelle with persistent open sutures
searchTerms: soft spot on head closes late
open head sutures longer than normal

pathognomonic.symptomName: Multiple supernumerary teeth with delayed eruption

common.symptomName: Hypoplastic maxilla leading to midface hypoplasia
Narrow thorax with pectus excavatum or carinatum

occasional.symptomName: Hearing loss due to middle ear abnormalities
searchTerms: hearing loss from ear bone problems

occasional.symptomName: Delayed motor milestones due to skeletal abnormalities
searchTerms: slow motor skill development due to bone problems
late crawling or walking from skeletal issues

occasional.symptomName: Dental caries secondary to abnormal dentition

rare.symptomName: Craniosynostosis in isolated cranial ossification defect cases
Conductive hearing loss due to ossicular chain malformations
searchTerms: hearing loss from ear bone malformation

rare.symptomName: Increased intracranial pressure secondary to cranial defects

laboratory: Genetic testing showing RUNX2 gene mutation
imaging: Radiographs showing absent or hypoplastic clavicles
Delayed ossification of cranial sutures and fontanelles
Dental panoramic X-rays revealing supernumerary teeth
genetic: Heterozygous pathogenic variants in RUNX2 gene (chromosome 6p21)
other: Family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Clinical examination revealing hypermobility of shoulders due to clavicular hypoplasia

distinguishingFeatures: Delayed closure of cranial sutures but normal clavicles

redFlags: Progressive neurological symptoms suggesting increased intracranial pressure
Severe respiratory compromise due to thoracic deformity
Failure to thrive or severe feeding difficulties secondary to craniofacial abnormalities
references: Mundlos S. Cleidocranial dysplasia: clinical and molecular genetics. J Med Genet. 1999;36(3):177-182.
